complexity.time: O(log n) with index, O(n) without
complexity.explanation: Without an index, the database engine must evaluate the predicate across all n table rows via an O(n) sequential scan. A B-Tree index organizes keys in balanced hierarchical nodes, achieving O(log n) search time at the cost of O(n) auxiliary tree storage.

executionTrace.memoryDetail: The database engine checks every row for a match, streaming all 10,000 table pages from disk into memory.
Sorts table keys and allocates hierarchical B-Tree nodes mapping each email string to its rowid pointer.
The B-Tree root points to the correct leaf node in 2-3 page hops, directly retrieving rowid 8472.

pitfalls.title: Index Bloat: Over-Indexing Slows Write Operations
pitfalls.description: Creating too many indexes slows down INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations because every write must update the B-Tree structure and maintain key balance.
pitfalls.goodSnippet:
-- Index only high-cardinality columns frequently queried in WHERE or JOIN clauses
CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);

pitfalls.title: Wrong Column: Indexing Unfiltered Attributes
pitfalls.description: Indexing a column that is not used in WHERE, JOIN, or ORDER BY clauses consumes memory without improving query execution time.

seniorInterviewTip: Indexes make reads fast but writes slow. Every INSERT must update the B-Tree. In production, profile your slow queries with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before adding indexes.
